picks.file: Coventry Cathedral, 1957, view from ruined nave to Holy Trinity spire - geograph.org.uk - 4601206.jpg
picks.what: The ruined cathedral and the spire of Holy Trinity, photograph
picks.why: the city’s defining landmark scene; marked as an event because the cathedral was bombed in 1940

picks.what: View east from the cathedral tower over the ruined old cathedral, photograph
picks.why: high, sharp panorama of the center with the cathedral ruins in front

gaps: P0–P2: nothing; P4: nothing; P3 has only one view (#1 is a single building, St Mary’s Hall)
notes: #4 is marked event so the bombed cathedral is not shown for years before 1957; if that is too strict, #6 (1967 general view from Priory Hall, no landmarks) is the alternative for P5. #9 (2010 aerial) has heavily oversaturated color. Leicester’s candidate #3 (‘The antiquities of Warwickshire illustrated…’ fleuron, 1730 second edition of Dugdale) is actually two prospects of Coventry; it could fill P2 here if it is added to Coventry’s candidates.
